title: Daytona org ECR registry credentials expire (12h) — document refresh procedure
description: During Aug 23 snapshot roll, all 3 stored org registry entries (aws-ecr-us-east-1) had expired ECR tokens causing 'denied: Your authorization token has expired' on snapshot builds. Fixed by PATCH /docker-registry/{id} with fresh aws ecr get-login-password (full body: name/url/username/password/project required). title: Portal Agents/Channels IA
description:
Portal IA for durable agents, channels, and killing Projects in the UI.

Normative lock: docs/plans/0016-agents-channels-ia/decision-locked-ia.md
Plan: docs/plans/0016-agents-channels-ia/
Integration branch: integrate/lac-bx3
Sibling harness epic: lac-bx3 in lanyard-agent (session keys, hop cap, prompt layers).

v1: one human, many agents. Multi-human later.

## Success Criteria
1. Sidenav is Channels / Agents / Scheduled Tasks. No Projects UI.
2. Agents row is the durable agent; one persistent 1:1; New agent mints a person not a clone.
3. Channel requires a name and ≥2 agents; floor two after create; @ wakes only in channels; un-mentioned mail goes to lead.
4. Delete agent confirms and removes channel membership and job binds. Delete channel keeps agents.
5. Legacy interactive chats migrate 1:1 → one agent; no auto-channels.
6. I1-I16 in docs/plans/0016-agents-channels-ia/testing.md green (BFF units + Playwright).
notes: Sibling harness epic lac-bx3 in lanyard-agent. Integration branch integrate/lac-bx3 in both repos. Locked IA: docs/plans/0016-agents-channels-ia/decision-locked-ia.md
close_reason: All 14 children closed. Buzz cutover IA shipped on integrate/lac-bx3: sidenav Channels/Agents/Scheduled Tasks (Projects gone), durable agents with persistent 1:1, channels with floor-two + lead + succession, @ wake only in channels, delete-agent cascade, scheduled tasks bind one agent, legacy migration, full Playwright catalog green on the live stack (real LA harness + LiteLLM path). Follow-up: lp-ighv (persona speaker/prompt on harness hop).

title: /admin: entitle tenants to google, hubspot, whatsapp
description:
Why: Lanyard ops grants the tenant the catalog, never signs in. Design: docs/architecture/portal-connectors.md §2. Depends on lp-2qs ops session (/admin).
Ops UI/API: tenant may use connector ids. Cross-tenant status counts. No OAuth, no QR, no sticky edits.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] /admin can toggle tenant entitlement for the three v1 connectors
[ ] Tenant cookie cannot call this API
[ ] Entitlement off triggers lifecycle delete (dep on lifecycle slice)
[ ] Smoke: ops session vs tenant session
notes:
Playbook: feature.md

architect skipped: design frozen in docs/architecture/portal-connectors.md §2–3 and dual-auth-credential-planes.md. Two shapes: (A) BFF /api/admin ops-gated catalog + toggle, CP SoT with entitlement-off deleting connection rows, /admin SPA on the web tarball; (B) tenant /api/connectors with an ops impersonation flag or Prisma @lanyard/admin. Picked A (ops cookie plane, no OAuth/QR/sticky, CP stays private).

Throughput checkpoint:
- Blocking first steps: typed catalog (tenant × connector entitlement + status counts), then CP delete-on-off, then BFF ops gate, then /admin page.
- Independent workstreams: n/a (one ops surface).
- Shared mutable state: CP entitlement + connection rows; one writer (CP PUT). Guest disks are per sandbox.
- Smallest safe decomposition: one worker; catalog, toggle, and fail-closed session are one artifact.

Principles: model-the-domain (ConnectorCatalog table, not per-tenant ifs), foundational-thinking (types first), laziness (reuse ops session + CP upsert; no second ALB), redesign-from-first-principles (ops entitlement is not a tenant admin grant), boundary-discipline (ops cookie at /api/admin; parse ConnectorId at HTTP), type-system-discipline (closed ConnectorId; ops DTO has no secrets/OAuth/QR/sticky), prove-it-works (ops vs tenant session smoke + entitlement-off deletes rows), build-the-lever (integration suite is the rerunnable proof), separate-before-serializing-shared-state (n/a isolated worktree).
Draft PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/583 sha bf588971. Tests: CP connector-catalog + connectors.integration (entitlement-off deletes secrets); BFF ops-connectors unit+integration (tenant cookie 401, ops toggle, OAuth blocked); web opsConnectors parse/fetch/page toggle. needs_ui_qa=true (/admin SPA).
Re-verified on existing branch bf588971 / PR #583. CP 851 tests pass (catalog + entitlement-off delete). BFF ops-connectors unit+integration pass (tenant cookie 401, ops toggle deletes secrets, ops cannot OAuth). Web opsConnectors parse + OpsConnectorsPage toggle pass. No additional commit. needs_ui_qa=true.
close_reason: Merged https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/583 (e47ebb96). /admin entitles google/hubspot/whatsapp; tenant cookie 401; entitlement-off deletes secrets; UI QA passed.

title: Scheduled tasks that use connectors run as that user
description:

Jobs that need google/hubspot/whatsapp bind owner_user_id, wake that user sandbox, use that connection row. Tenant-scoped cron cannot use those connectors in v1.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Creating a Gmail-using scheduled task stores user id
[ ] Fire path ensure_online user instance, not tenant primary
[ ] Tenant sandbox job cannot inject user connector secrets
[ ] Test or proof with a draft-only gws job
notes:
Playbook: feature.md.
architect skipped: design frozen in docs/architecture/portal-connectors.md §4 last paragraph. Two shapes: (A) persist owner_user_id+connector_ids at create and retarget fire to the user sandbox; (B) run tenant cron with impersonated tokens. Picked A so tenant sandbox never sees Alice Gmail.

Throughput:

- Independent workstreams: n/a (one create+fire artifact).
- Shared mutable state: per-user instance + connection row; guest disks split by sandbox_id.

Principles: model-the-domain (ScheduledTaskConnectorNeed none|user_principal), foundational-thinking (types before fire branches), laziness (reuse injectUserConnector + ensureUserSandbox), redesign-from-first-principles (fire target is owner sandbox, not a tenant special case), boundary-discipline (detect/bind at create; inject refuses tenant), type-system-discipline (tenant+gmail unrepresentable), prove-it-works (draft-only gws job: create stores user, fire wakes user instance, tenant inject throws), build-the-lever (detect table is the rerunnable classifier), separate-before-serializing-shared-state (Alice vs tenant guest disks).
Verified existing branch 5bfd6917 + draft PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/571. Acceptance covered: Gmail create stamps owner_user_id; fire ensure_online user instance; tenant inject throws; draft-only gws fixture. Tests: CP scheduled-task-connectors (10) + harness-scheduled-task-create (9) + fire.integration (5) + harness-fire (2) + schedule-evaluator (12); BFF scheduled-task-connectors (3) + settings-scheduled-tasks-harness (5). No additional commit.

title: Lifecycle: disconnect, refresh, needs_reauth, entitlement-off deletes secrets
description:
Why: leftover tokens after role-off are a breach. Design: docs/architecture/portal-connectors.md §7.
User Disconnect deletes row + provider revoke / wacli auth logout. Refresh rotates; failure → needs_reauth not delete. Role or tenant entitlement off deletes those rows. User removed from tenant deletes all their connection rows. Audit metadata only.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Disconnect google: row gone, revoke attempted, inject cache dropped
[ ] Grant off google for role: those users' google rows gone
[ ] Refresh fail: status needs_reauth, wizard, row remains
[ ] Tests for each event in the lifecycle table
notes:
Playbook: feature.md.
architect skipped: design frozen in docs/architecture/portal-connectors.md §7. Two shapes: (A) bolt revoke/delete onto existing grant upsert and DELETE; (B) first-class lifecycle event table + apply. Picked B so each table row is one event kind and tests are table-driven.

Throughput:
- Blocking first steps: lifecycle table (event → row/provider/sandbox), apply with ports.
- Independent workstreams: n/a (one reducer; CP row is the shared write).
- Shared mutable state: CP connection row is the one write target; guest disks split by sandbox_id.
- Smallest safe decomposition: one worker; grant-off/entitlement-off/disconnect/refresh/user-removed share apply.

Principles: model-the-domain (ConnectorLifecycleEvent table), foundational-thinking (plan before IO), laziness (reuse delete/upsert/inject store), redesign-from-first-principles (grant-off deletes only users who lose access), boundary-discipline (OAuth revoke/refresh at provider port), type-system-discipline (refresh_fail cannot delete), prove-it-works (unit + CP/BFF/SPA tests), build-the-lever (table + apply is the rerunnable proof), separate-before-serializing-shared-state (per-user CP row + per-sandbox guest cache).
close_reason: Lifecycle table + apply shipped on 5c5825fe. Draft PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/572. Disconnect google deletes the row, attempts revoke, and drops inject cache. Grant/entitlement off deletes leftover secrets. Refresh fail sets needs_reauth, keeps the row, and shows Reconnect. Tests: CP lifecycle unit + Postgres integration, BFF connectors.integration, SPA SettingsView Disconnect/Reconnect.

title: HubSpot OAuth, six CRM objects, sticky portal pin
description:
Why: first-cut CRM. Design: docs/architecture/portal-connectors.md §1, §3 HubSpot.
Runtimes api+cli+skill. Scopes: contacts, companies, deals, notes, tasks, meetings + identity. First connect pins hubspot_portal_id; mismatch rejected; admin can clear pin. Same OAuth/approval/inject machinery as Google.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] HubSpot row Connect works with Lanyard app
[ ] First connect sets tenant pin; second user wrong portal fails closed
[ ] Clear pin does not delete tokens
[ ] hubspot.write is every_call; hubspot.read can sticky
[ ] Tests: pin mismatch, grant off deletes row
notes:
Playbook: feature.md
architect skipped: design frozen in docs/architecture/portal-connectors.md §3 HubSpot scopes, §5 OAuth, §7 pin/grant-off. Two shapes: (A) BFF owns PKCE + HubSpot authorize URL; CP exchanges code, evaluates sticky portal pin, writes KMS ciphertext; (B) BFF exchanges HubSpot tokens then PUTs secrets and pin. Picked A so SPA and BFF never hold refresh tokens and pin is a tenant-owned CP invariant.

Throughput:
- Blocking first steps: HubSpot CRM scope table, pin decision ADT, PKCE state bind.
- Independent workstreams: n/a (one OAuth + pin flow).
- Shared mutable state: tenant hubspot_portal_id is the pin write; connection rows are per-user; guest disks split by sandbox_id.
- Smallest safe decomposition: one worker; start/callback/pin/CP write/inject are one artifact.

Principles: model-the-domain (HubSpotTokenGrant + HubSpotPinDecision, not scattered query params), foundational-thinking (scopes+pin types before routes), laziness (reuse session HMAC + CP upsert/inject), redesign-from-first-principles (pin lives on entitlement; first connect writes it; mismatch is unrepresentable as connected), boundary-discipline (parse token+token-info at HubSpot edge; SPA JSON allowlist), type-system-discipline (hubspot.write cannot be sticky; pin mismatch is a typed error), prove-it-works (unit + Postgres BFF/CP integration), build-the-lever (scope/pin/grant parsers are the rerunnable proof), separate-before-serializing-shared-state (per-tenant pin vs per-user CP row).
Pushed a7b5261b. Draft PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/577. Acceptance: pin set/mismatch 409, clear pin keeps tokens, grant off deletes row, hubspot.write every_call. Tests: CP hubspot-oauth 11 + integration 5; BFF hubspot 4+4; existing CP connectors 9; BFF connectors.integration 5; web connectors/SettingsView/PortalShell.
Verified on existing branch a7b5261b / PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/577. No extra commit. Pin mismatch 409, clear pin keeps tokens, grant off deletes row, hubspot.write every_call. Playbook feature.md; architect skipped (design frozen).

title: MCP invoke: harness stdio/HTTP; vault stdio session is out of v1
description:
Follow docs/architecture/short-stack-tool-placement.md.

HTTP/SSE MCP and stdio MCP that do not need the vault run on the harness (McpStdioClient). search_tool / use_tool keep hidden tools off LiteLLM tools[].

stdio MCP that must see /mnt/vault is NOT toolbox process/execute (JSON-RPC session, not one argv). Do not fake it. Track a Daytona process-session bind separately if a tenant needs vault MCP.

Live catalog seed remains lp-jzfc.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] use_tool can invoke at least one harness MCP (lab_echo or HTTP) on MockLab after lp-jzfc seed.
- [ ] Vault-required stdio MCP is fail-closed honest, not toolbox execute.
- [ ] Guest create-env has no MCP secrets dumped into the sandbox.
notes:
Playbook: feature.md. architect skipped: precedent is McpStdioClient (lp-zuh.14.3) + createEnvToolsTurnRunner catalog bind (lp-oop.38.6). Two shapes: (A) wire agent-core ToolCatalog/prepareToolsForModel into the LiteLLM runner; (B) runner-local discriminated McpPlacement + search_tool/use_tool (picked — harness loop is LiteLLM ToolSchema, not Pi AgentTool). Throughput: blocking=classify placement + denylist; independent=LA invoke vs platform create-env; shared state=tools-runner.ts serial, create-env serial; smallest decomp=one MCP invoke module + denylist predicate.
Platform PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-platform/pull/559 (fa2bce71). LA PR https://github.com/LanyardBrain/lanyard-agent/pull/256 (a69f31a). Tests: CP create-env 10 pass; validate.sh 63 pass; LA config 118, mcp 5, harness-mcp+runner 25. Live MockLab invoke N/A until lp-jzfc seed + harness image roll. Follow-up lp-oop.38.19 process-session bind.
